title: Singapore Retail Supplier Delivery Risk
thesis: Every inbound truckload or container from a supplier to a Singapore distribution centre of Lantern Bay Grocers, a fictional grocery and general-merchandise retailer, either arrives by the PO commit date or it does not. Snowflake turns those deliveries into on-time and flag-precision KPIs, a 7-day delivery-miss risk score per supplier, ASN quantity variance anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

persona.name: Farah Iskandar
persona.role: Head of Supplier Management, Lantern Bay Grocers (fictional)

talking_points: Start with the question a category buyer asks: how many of the cases our suppliers shipped arrived on time? 40 suppliers dispatching from 8 Singapore planning areas, from Tuas and Pasir Panjang in the west to Changi and Tampines in the east, in 5 product categories from fresh produce to household goods.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to supplier-day rows.
The exception-signal chart shows which checks lead to confirmed delivery misses and which mostly produce false-positive flags.
show: Daily inbound shipments and exception flags
tabs.call_out: One governed definition of on-time delivery, from supplier dispatch to DC receiving

transition.line: Which suppliers should the replenishment team call first?

persona.name: Marcus Teo
persona.role: Inbound Replenishment Lead, Lantern Bay Grocers (fictional)

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification ranks suppliers by the probability of a confirmed delivery miss in the next 7 days, so follow-up goes where it matters.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags ASN quantity variance outliers per supplier, and the forecast projects network-wide inbound shipments for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are supplier reviews and alternate suppliers keeping up?

persona.name: Marcus Teo
persona.role: Inbound Replenishment Lead, Lantern Bay Grocers (fictional)

talking_points: Supplier review completion, alternate-supplier coverage and approvals still pending.
The scatter compares each supplier's review completion with its confirmed delivery misses.
tabs.call_out: Close alternate-supplier gaps before an allocation cut empties the shelf

transition.line: What happens when a shipment arrives out of tolerance?

persona.name: Marcus Teo
persona.role: Inbound Replenishment Lead, Lantern Bay Grocers (fictional)

talking_points: Inbound-shipment events land in RAW.LIVE_SHIPMENTS: simulated in Snowflake, or from Amazon Data Firehose through S3 and Snowpipe in the AWS build.
FLAG events (a delivery whose ASN quantity variance is out of tolerance) are logged by the alert, which emails the inbound replenishment team.
tabs.call_out: From supplier dispatch to receiving-dock alert in one platform

persona.name: Farah Iskandar
persona.role: Head of Supplier Management, Lantern Bay Grocers (fictional)

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers with generated SQL over the semantic view and cites the synthetic delivery-exception SOPs by ID.
The action memo is drafted only from KPI, supplier, exception-signal and risk rows; exception checks are demo signals, not supplier audit or compliance verdicts.
show: Agent answer with SQL and SOP citations
tabs.call_out: Answers carry their SQL and SOP IDs, so nobody has to trust a number blindly

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

persona.name: Farah Iskandar
persona.role: Head of Supplier Management, Lantern Bay Grocers (fictional)

talking_points: Both builds share the same core: seeded data, dynamic tables, Snowflake ML, Cortex Search, semantic view, agent, alert and task graph.
The AWS build adds Amazon Data Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe ingestion, a Bedrock memo and a QuickSight dashboard with an Amazon Q topic.
